headline: ChatGPT will show picture ads while it makes your images
summary: OpenAI is testing picture ads in ChatGPT's image maker, starting in the US. UK Free and Go users already see text ads, and you can limit what they know about you.
body: OpenAI announced a new kind of ChatGPT ad on 5 October: pictures that show a product in use, placed beside an image ChatGPT is making for you. OpenAI says the ads carry a clear label and stay separate from your image. Testing starts later this month in the US, for people on the Free and Go plans.

UK users already see ChatGPT's text ads. They started rolling out here in June, under some answers, for Free and Go users. Plus and Pro stay ad-free, and OpenAI says it shows no ads to accounts it identifies as under 18. OpenAI hasn't said when picture ads will reach the UK.
OpenAI says ads never change ChatGPT's answers and advertisers never see your chats. Advertisers get totals such as views and clicks.
do_this: Open Settings, then Ads controls. Switch off personalised ads, and stop past chats and memory shaping the ads you see.
Use Temporary Chat for anything private. It shows no ads.
On the Free plan, you can go ads-free from Ads controls. The catch: fewer messages and no image making.

social.Topic: ChatGPT will show picture ads while it makes your images, US test first
social.Caption Notes:
ChatGPT is about to show picture ads while it makes your images. OpenAI announced the new format on 5 October. Testing starts later this month in the US, for people on the Free and Go plans.

In the UK, Free and Go users already see text ads under some answers. They arrived in June. Plus and Pro stay ad-free, and OpenAI says it shows no ads to under-18s.

OpenAI says ads never change ChatGPT's answers and advertisers never see your chats. You still decide how much the ads know about you:

• Open Settings > Ads controls. Switch off personalised ads, and stop past chats and memory shaping them.
• Use Temporary Chat for anything private. It shows no ads.
• On Free, you can go ads-free. The catch: fewer messages and no image making.

Follow @ainofluff for more plain-English AI updates.

Source: OpenAI, 5 Oct 2026.
